hints: Focus on whether oxidation numbers actually change, which means one species is oxidised while the other is reduced.
Identify each reaction type first: alkene plus bromine, alcohol plus concentrated acid, carbonyl plus HCN, and ester plus dilute acid.
Check which change joins atoms with a change in oxidation state, with $\text{Br}_2$ going from 0 to -1, and pick that pair.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes a redox reaction**

Remember, redox means oxidation numbers change. One reactant is oxidised (oxidation number increases) and the other is reduced (oxidation number decreases).

Rule to use:
$$\text{redox if oxidation numbers change, not redox if they stay the same}$$

**Name the four reaction types**

Let's be a detective and name each one. A is electrophilic addition of $\text{Br}_2$ to the alkene $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$. B is dehydration of the alcohol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ to an alkene. C is nucleophilic addition of $\text{HCN}$ to the ketone $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$. D is acid hydrolysis of the ester $\text{HCO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$.

**Test A for oxidation number change**

In $\text{Br}_2$, each Br is 0. In the dibromo product $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{Br}$, each Br is -1, so bromine is reduced. The $\text{C=C}$ carbons gain more electronegative Br atoms, so carbon is oxidised. That is redox:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{Br}$$

**Confirm B, C and D have no redox**

Dehydration, cyanohydrin formation and ester hydrolysis only rearrange bonds between C, H, O and N without changing oxidation numbers. No element is oxidised or reduced, so they are elimination, addition and hydrolysis, but not redox.

options.A: Correct. Addition of $\text{Br}_2$ to propene is redox. Bromine is reduced from 0 in $\text{Br}_2$ to -1 in the C-Br bonds, while the alkene carbons are oxidised as they bond to more electronegative bromine.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ undergoes dehydration to propene plus water. This is an elimination (acid catalysed), oxidation numbers of C, H and O do not change, so it is not redox.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ with $\text{HCN}$ undergoes nucleophilic addition to form a cyanohydrin. No oxidation numbers change, the carbonyl carbon stays at the same oxidation level, so it is not redox.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{HCO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ undergoes acid hydrolysis to methanoic acid plus ethanol. This is a substitution at the acyl group with no change in oxidation numbers, so it is not redox.
